item.title: W34 Tuesday
item.dc:creator: Samson Wang
item.description:
1 ostentatious

[ ˌästənˈtāshəs ]
(adj.) Ostentatious describes someone or something that displays wealth, knowledge, power, etc., in a way that is meant to attract attention, admiration, or envy. Things that are ostentatious tend to stand out as overly elaborate or conspicuous.

The resort town is famous for its extravagantly expensive summer homes, which some tourists view as impressive and others merely ostentatious.

2 ductile

[ ˈdəktəl ]
(adj.) capable of being drawn out into wire or thread; easily led or influenced; capable of being fashioned into a new form.

The web-like blue and gold dial is housed in a 40mm case made of tantalum, a very hard, ductile, lustrous, blue-gray transition metal that is highly corrosion-resistant.
例句中的 dail 在这里的含义是表盘。

3 synonym

[ ˈsinəˌnim ]
(n.) one of two or more words or expressions of the same language that have the same or nearly the same meaning in some or all senses.

The debris hurtled by so fast that the New York Times editorial page seemed to run out of synonyms for disgust, revulsion and abuse.

4 corrosion

[ kəˈrōzhən ]
(n.) the action, process, or effect of corroding

The corrosion of family values that is often brought on by great wealth.

5 lustrous

[ ˈləstrəs ]
(adj.) reflecting light evenly and efficiently without glitter or sparkle

The lustrous finish on the satin bedspread adds to the feeling of luxury.

6 debris

[ dəˈbrē ]
(n.) the remains of something broken down or destroyed.

After the earthquake, rescuers began digging through the debris in search of survivors.

7 extravagantly

[ ikˈstravigənt ]
(adj.) exceeding the limits of reason or necessity

The company has been making extravagant claims about the drug's effectiveness.

8 conspicuous

[ kənˈspikyəwəs ]
(adj.) obvious to the eye or mind

There were a number of conspicuous changes to the building.

9 prominent

[ ˈprämənənt ]
(adj.) standing out or projecting beyond a surface or line

He quickly became prominent in the music industry.

10 leverage

[ ˈlevərij ]
(n.) the action of a lever or the mechanical advantage gained by it
(vt.) to provide (something, such as a corporation) or supplement (something, such as money) with leverage

The union's size gave it leverage in the labor contract negotiations.
The company wants to leverage its brands more effectively.

（全文完）

item.title: W34 Monday
item.dc:creator: Samson Wang
item.description:
1 dampen

[ ˈdampən ]
(vt.) to check or diminish the activity or vigor
The heat dampened our spirits.

2 cull

[ ˈkəl ]
(v.) to select from a group
Damaged fruits are culled before the produce is shipped.

(v.) to reduce or control the size of (something, such as a herd) by removal (as by hunting or slaughter) of especially weak or sick individuals
The town issued hunting licenses in order to cull the deer population.

3 sodium

[ ˈsō-dē-əm ]
(n.) a silver-white soft waxy ductile element of the alkali metal group with atomic number 11 that occurs abundantly in nature in combined form and is very active chemically
钠

alkali 碱
sodium chloride 氯化钠，chloride 氯化物

4 amino

[ əˈmēˌnō ]
(adj.) relating to, being, or containing an amine group
氨基
amino acid 氨基酸

5 protein

[ ˈprōˌtēn ]
(n.) any of various naturally occurring extremely complex substances that consist of amino-acid residues joined by peptide bonds, contain the elements carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, usually sulfur, and occasionally other elements (such as phosphorus or iron), and include many essential biological compounds (such as enzymes, hormones, or antibodies)
蛋白质

6 antihistamine

[ ˌantēˈhistəˌmēn ]
(n.) any of various compounds that counteract histamine in the body and that are used for treating allergic reactions (such as hay fever) and cold symptoms
抗组胺药

7 sprinkle

[ ˈspriŋkəl ]
(v.) to scatter in drops or particles
He sprinkled water on the plants.

8 clump

[ ˈkləmp ]
(n.) a group of things clustered together
There is a clump of bushes at the edge of the field.

9 dietetics

[ ˌdīəˈtetiks ]
(n.) the science or art of applying the principles of nutrition to the diet
营养学

10 shun

[ ˈshən ]
(v.) to avoid deliberately and especially habitually
He shuns parties and social events.

（全文完）

item.title: W33 Tuseday
item.dc:creator: Samson Wang
item.description:
1 palatable

[ ˈpælətəbl ]
(adj.) (of food or drink) pleasant to taste.
This is a very palatable local red wine.

2 ounce

[ ouns ]
(n.) a unit of weight of one sixteenth of a pound avoirdupois (approximately 28 grams).
Melt three ounces of butter in a large frying pan.

3 naringin

[ nəˈrinjə̇n ]
柚苷，柚皮苷
(n.) Naringin is a flavonoid, specifically a flavanone glycoside, found in citrus fruits like grapefruit, and known for its bitter taste.

4 antioxidant

[ ˌæntiˈɒksɪdənt ]
(n.) a substance that inhibits oxidation, especially one used to counteract the deterioration of stored food products
An antioxidant is a substance that prevents or slow down oxidation, a chemical reaction that produces harmful free radicals.

5 arteriosclerosis

[ ɑ:ˌtɪəriəʊskləˈrəʊsɪs ]
(n.) Arteriosclerosis is a type of vascular disease where the blood vessels carrying oxygen away from the heart (arteries) become damaged from factors such as high cholesterol, high blood pressure, diabetes and certain genetic influences.

6 miniature

[ ˈmɪnətʃə(r) ]
(adj.) (especially of a replica of something) of a much smaller size than normal; very small.
Children dressed as miniature adults.

(n.) a thing that is much smaller than normal, especially a small replica or model.
Seven full-size car bodies and three miniatures were used.

(v.) represent on a smaller scale; reduce to miniature dimensions.
She saw her own reflection miniatured.

7 cleanse

[ klenz ]
(vt.) to rid of impurities by or as if by washing
It's that mystical state most athletes are lucky to achieve a few times in their careers. The mind is cleansed. The body is free.

8 citrus

[ ˈsi-trəs ]
(n.) any of a group of often thorny trees and shrubs (Citrus and related genera) of the rue family grown in warm regions for their edible fruit (such as the orange or lemon) with firm usually thick rind and pulpy flesh.
Go back in time and connect with nature at Neapolis Archeological Park, which has an ancient Greek theater, Roman amphitheater, and centuries-old citrus trees.

9 cruciferous

[ /ˈkrüsəfər / ]
(n.) any of a family (Brassicaceae synonym Cruciferae) of plants including the cabbage, turnip, and mustard
十字花科的
brussel sprout 芽球甘蓝

10 quinine

[ ˈkwīˌnīn ]
(n.) a salt of quinine used especially as an antipyretic, antimalarial, and bitter tonic
奎宁
Tonic water is sweetend soda that contains bitter-tasting chemcial compound called quinie.

（全文完）

item.title: Week33 Monday
item.dc:creator: Samson Wang
item.description:
1 ubiquitous

[ ju:ˈbɪkwɪtəs ]
(v.) - present everywhere
Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern society.

2 exacerbate

[ ɪgˈzæsəbeɪt ]
(v.) - to make a problem worse
Poor urban planing exacerbates traffic congestion.

3 ephemeral

[ ɪˈfemərəl ]
(adj.) - lasting for a very short time
Social media trends are often ephemeral.

4 pragmatic

[ prægˈmætɪk ]
(v.) - dealing with things sensibly and realistically
A pragmatic approach to education focus on practical skills.

5 resilient

[ rɪˈzɪliənt ]
(adj.) - able to recover from difficulties
Children are often more resilient than adults think.

6 detrimental

[ ˌdetrɪˈmentl ]
(adj.) - harmful or damaging
Lack of sleep can be detrimental to health.

7 inevitable

[ ɪnˈevɪtəbl ]
(adj.) - certain to happen, unavoidable
Technological advancement is inevitable in the 21st centuary.

8 conducive

[ kənˈdju:sɪv ]
(adj.) - making a certain situation likely or possible.
A quiet environment is conducive to effective studying.

9 paradigm

[ ˈpærədaɪm ]
(n.) - typical example or pattern
The internet caused a paradigm shift in communication.

10 precursor

[ pri:ˈkɜ:sə(r) ]
(n.) - something that comes before
The telegraph was a precursor to modern communications.

（全文完）

item.title: Week32 Friday
item.dc:creator: Samson Wang
item.description:
1 mitigate

[ ˈmɪtɪgeɪt ]
(v.) - make less severe
Planting trees helps mitigate the effects of climate change.

2 proliferation

[ prəˌlɪfəˈreɪʃn ]
(n.) - rapid increase
The proliferation of fast food has contributed to health problems.

3 precarious

[ prɪˈkeəriəs ]
(adj.) - dangerously unstable
Many workers face precarious employment conditions.

4 corroborate

[ kəˈrɒbəreɪt ]
(v.) - confirm with evidence
The witness testimony corroborated the defendant's story.

5 discretionary

[ dɪˈskreʃənəri ]
(adj.) - available for optional use
The company offers discretionary bonuses for exceptional work.

6 exemplary

[ ɪgˈzempləri ]
(adj.) - serving as a desirable model
The student showed exemplary behavior throughout the year.

7 facilitate

[ fəˈsɪlɪteɪt ]
(v.) - make easier
Technology facilitates global communication.

8 inconsequential

[ ɪnˌkɒnsɪˈkwenʃl ]
(adj.) - unimportant
The spelling mistake was inconsequential to the overall meaning.

9 novel

[ ˈnɒvl ]
(adj.) - new and original
The scientist proposed a novel approach to the problem.

10 stringent

[ ˈstrɪndʒənt ]
(adj.) - strict and precise
The university has stringent admission requirements.

（全文完）
